title: PPE, respiratory protection and worker readiness
audience: Supervisors, coordinators and trained cleaners who may be asked to triage, refer or document mould-related work in homes, rentals and commercial buildings, under an approved plan. Not a qualification or authority to remediate, demolish, or certify any building or room.
learningOutcomes: Match a described exposure to the PPE set out in the approved plan, and identify an unsuitable choice.
Stop a worker who is not ready, and record the reason.
Complete a PPE readiness check for a fictional crew.

instruction.heading: Scope of this lesson
instruction.body: This lesson covers selecting and checking PPE. It does not replace an exposure assessment, a respirator programme or the fit of a respirator, and it does not clear a worker to enter a contaminated area.

instruction.heading: What the guideline sets as minimum points
instruction.body: The WA Department of Health guideline says the respiratory tract, eyes and skin must be protected during remediation. Its PPE appendix says a P2 or N95 respirator face-mask should be worn to reduce exposure to airborne mould spores, and that powered air-purifying respirators should be used when remediating complex mould situations. These are minimum points for mould work in Western Australia. The approved plan sets the actual selection for each job, based on the exposure that has been assessed.

instruction.heading: Readiness before entry
instruction.body: Before anyone enters a contaminated area, confirm the respirator programme, the worker's training and the fit of the respirator. A worker who brings a loose disposable mask and says it is enough for major demolition has not met the requirement. Equipment does not replace exposure controls, and it cannot be relied on alone. Stop until a competent person has assessed the exposure, selected the equipment and confirmed that the worker is ready. Record each check, including the checks that failed.

procedure: Read the approved plan for the PPE selected for this exposure.
Confirm each worker's respirator programme, training and fit record.
Check that the PPE is in good condition before entry.
Put on and remove the PPE in the order the plan sets, in the designated area.
Stop any worker who is not ready, and record the reason.
Log the PPE check and the decision to proceed or stop.

workedExamples.situation: A worker brings a loose disposable mask and says it is enough for major demolition.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the worker ready to start?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Stop until a competent person has approved the PPE and the worker's readiness. The guideline's respirator points are minimums, and major demolition needs a plan-based selection.

workedExamples.situation: A complex job is planned, and the crew proposes standard paper masks for everyone.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The guideline says powered air-purifying respirators should be used for complex remediation. Refer to the competent supervisor for an approved selection before work starts.

equipmentAndPpe: PPE selection record tied to the approved plan.
Respirator programme records, training records and fit records for each worker.
Training-only PPE set. No real contaminated area is entered in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Wearing a loose disposable mask for a major job.
commonErrors.prevention: Match the PPE to the exposure, and verify the respirator programme, training and fit before entry.

commonErrors.error: Relying on a mask alone and skipping containment or cleaning controls.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat PPE as one control, within the approved plan.

commonErrors.error: Entering before training and fit are checked.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the readiness record for every worker before entry.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Respiratory protection depends on an employer's respirator programme and on the worker's training. Completing this lesson does not qualify a worker to use respiratory protection without that programme.
The PPE points come from the WA guideline and apply to mould in buildings in Western Australia. They are not a national standard.

qualityStandard: The learner matches a described exposure to the PPE in the plan, and identifies an unsuitable choice.
The learner stops a worker who is not ready, and records the reason.
The learner completes the PPE readiness check for a fictional crew.
documentationEvidence: PPE selection record tied to the approved plan.
Readiness record for each worker: training, respirator programme and fit.
Stop-or-proceed log for each PPE check.
summary: PPE follows the plan, not the other way round.
The respirator programme, training and fit are checked before entry.
A loose mask is not adequate for major work.
PPE is one control, not the only one.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker brings a loose disposable mask for a major demolition job. What is correct?
options: Stop until a competent person approves the PPE and the worker's readiness.
Let the worker start, because it is a mask.
Let the worker start with a second mask over the first.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the WA guideline say about respiratory protection for complex mould remediation?
options: Any paper dust mask is enough.
Powered air-purifying respirators should be used.
No respiratory protection is needed for complex remediation.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before a worker enters a contaminated area, which checks are needed?
options: A photograph of the worker's car.
The respirator programme, the worker's training and the fit.

officialReferences.title: Guidelines for managing mould and dampness: related public health risks in buildings (WA Department of Health)
officialReferences.pageDate: April 2024 (version control table); publication code ENV-0014702 MAY'24; no separate last-updated date shown
officialReferences.covers: Read through a page-summary tool on 2026-11-03 (PDF, Environmental Health Directorate, WA Department of Health). Section 1.4 sets out a general public health duty, a workplace duty and a residential tenancies duty. Section 2.1 names people with existing respiratory, immunocompromising and allergic conditions, and infants, children and older people. Section 3.2.2 says porous items are often not economically salvageable and must be thrown out. Section 3.3 says the source must be located to address the cause and prevent recurrence. Section 3.4.1 defines simple contamination as new, isolated and visible, no greater than one square metre, with easily identified causes, and its footnote calls the one-square-metre size arbitrary. Section 3.4.2 defines complex contamination as larger than one square metre or found in multiple rooms or places. Section 3.5 states there are no defined quantitative or qualitative exposure thresholds for mould or dampness. Section 4.1 lists containment, drying and source repair as principles. Section 4.2.2 advises scrubbing hard surfaces with soapy water, avoiding dry brushing, cleaning at least 30 to 50 cm beyond the visible mould, removing or discarding porous items that cannot be adequately cleaned, stating that mould is not considered hazardous waste, and not painting, sealing or covering surfaces until dry. Section 4.3 recommends a site-specific plan with professionals for complex contamination, isolation with heavy grade plastic and negative pressure, and evacuation of occupants. Section 4.4 lists no recurrence within two to four weeks after remediation as an indicator of success, recommends the evaluation be done by a different entity, and states there are no legal requirements for a post-remediation assessment. Appendix B recommends a P2 or N95 respirator and says PAPRs should be used for complex remediation. Appendix E says mould can grow within 24 to 48 hours in flood-affected homes.

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to remediate, demolish, disturb building materials, handle contaminated water or waste, or certify that a building, room or occupant area is safe or free of mould or pathogens. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Restricted or high-exposure remediation is carried out only by an appropriately qualified and competent professional under an approved plan, and some related work, including asbestos and lead disturbance and certain waste handling, is restricted to licensed or specially authorised people. The owner, manager, tenant or contract may define what work is permitted, but where the contract covers only routine cleaning, that is the limit of the task. Where the controlling authority or the competent supervisor is not identified, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: the hazards are unknown or changing; the work is destructive or hazardous and outside the authorised scope; exposure is uncontrolled or the building is unsafe to occupy; supervision, equipment or permissions are insufficient; flood, sewage, asbestos or lead may be present; a worker's PPE or respirator readiness has not been verified; a client asks for a clearance or pathogen-free statement; or a waste route is unauthorised. A stop-work decision is correct. Record it and restart only after the competent supervisor has confirmed the scope in writing.
